name: Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport
shortDescription: The world's busiest airport by passenger traffic and primary hub for Delta Air Lines.
description: Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport serves as the global mega-hub connecting the southeastern United States to major destinations worldwide. Featuring five parallel runways and two principal terminal complexes linked by the Automated People Mover (Plane Train), KATL handles more passenger movements annually than any other global airport.

name: Los Angeles International Airport
shortDescription: The primary international gateway to Southern California and major Pacific gateway.
description: Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) is a primary hub for more U.S. network carriers than any other airport. Positioned directly on the Pacific coastline, LAX plays a pivotal role in transatlantic, transpacific, and Latin American air traffic supported by nine interconnected terminal facilities.

name: Chicago O'Hare International Airport
shortDescription: Midwestern aviation powerhouse serving as a major hub for United and American Airlines.
description: Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD) features one of the most extensive multi-runway airfield configurations globally. Serving as a dual hub for United Airlines and American Airlines, O'Hare offers non-stop connectivity to major hubs across North America, Europe, Asia, and South America.

name: Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport
shortDescription: The primary operational mega-hub for American Airlines spanning over 17,000 acres.
description: Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) is the main hub for American Airlines and one of the largest land-area airports in the world. Operating seven active runways, DFW functions as a central transit gateway linking Latin America, North America, Europe, and Asia.

name: Denver International Airport
shortDescription: The largest airport by land area in North America, featuring the longest public runway in the US.
description: Denver International Airport (DEN) covers 53 square miles in Colorado. Elevated at over 5,000 feet above sea level, DEN uses a pinwheel layout of six long concrete runways—including the 16,000 ft Runway 16R/34L—to efficiently compensate for high-density altitude during warm summer months.

name: John F. Kennedy International Airport
shortDescription: The premier international air passenger gateway into the United States and New York Metro area.
description: John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) in Queens, New York, handles the highest volume of international air traffic entering North America. Serving dozens of foreign flag carriers, JFK connects the New York financial hub to virtually every major continent.

name: Miami International Airport
shortDescription: The primary Latin American air hub and major international freight center in the US.
description: Miami International Airport (MIA) acts as the main bridge between North America, Latin America, and the Caribbean. Holding a dominant share of international air freight in the US, MIA serves as American Airlines' primary Latin American operational nexus.

name: San Francisco International Airport
shortDescription: The main Pacific Northwest and Northern California hub for international and transpacific routes.
description: San Francisco International Airport (SFO) operates a distinctive intersecting runway layout on San Francisco Bay. Serving as United Airlines' flagship transpacific hub, SFO offers extensive non-stop connectivity to major innovation hubs across Asia-Pacific and Europe.

name: Seattle-Tacoma International Airport
shortDescription: The primary commercial gateway to the Pacific Northwest and home hub for Alaska Airlines.
description: Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (Sea-Tac) serves the Greater Seattle metropolitan region. Acting as the primary hub for Alaska Airlines and a transpacific gateway for Delta Air Lines, KSEA links North America directly to East Asia, Europe, and Alaska.

name: Toronto Pearson International Airport
shortDescription: Canada's largest and busiest airport, serving as Air Canada's primary global mega-hub.
description: Toronto Pearson International Airport (CYYZ) handles the largest volume of international traffic in Canada. Operating five runways across two major terminal buildings (Terminals 1 & 3), Pearson features US Preclearance facilities and links Southern Ontario to global destinations.

name: Vancouver International Airport
shortDescription: Canada's premier transpacific gateway on Sea Island in Richmond, British Columbia.
description: Vancouver International Airport (CYVR) sits on Sea Island in Metro Vancouver. Consistently awarded top honors for passenger experience in North America, YVR serves as Air Canada's chief transpacific portal connecting Canada with Asia, Oceania, and Europe.

name: Mexico City International Airport
shortDescription: Latin America's busiest airport by passenger traffic, situated in high-altitude Mexico City.
description: Benito Juárez International Airport (MMMX) is the primary commercial airport serving Greater Mexico City. Located at over 7,300 feet of altitude, it operates two parallel long asphalt runways handling domestic connectivity across Mexico alongside international long-haul routes to the Americas and Europe.

name: London Heathrow Airport
shortDescription: Europe's busiest airport and primary global hub for British Airways and Virgin Atlantic.
description: London Heathrow Airport (EGLL) is Europe's premier international gateway. Operating under strict noise quota restrictions in West London, its two high-intensity parallel runways achieve remarkable movement efficiency, hosting transoceanic long-haul flights connecting Europe to every continent.

name: Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport
shortDescription: France's flagship international hub and primary hub for Air France and FedEx European Express.
description: Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport (Roissy) features a parallel dual-runway layout designed for simultaneous independent takeoffs and landings. Serving as Air France's global home hub and FedEx Express's main European logistics center, CDG connects Europe with Africa, Asia, and the Americas.

name: Frankfurt Airport
shortDescription: Germany's main aviation gateway and primary operational mega-hub for Lufthansa.
description: Frankfurt Airport (EDDF) is a premier European aviation and cargo hub managed by Fraport. Centered around four operational runways—including the specialized Startbahn West (Runway 18)—FRA powers Lufthansa's global Star Alliance network with intermodal high-speed rail integration.

name: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol
shortDescription: Below sea-level single-terminal mega-hub and primary home of KLM Royal Dutch Airlines.
description: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (EHAM) utilizes a unique single-terminal concept supported by six operational runways (including the distant 'Polderbaan'). Situated 11 feet below sea level, Schiphol acts as the primary global hub for SkyTeam partner KLM.

name: Adolfo Suárez Madrid–Barajas Airport
shortDescription: Spain's largest airport and the essential bridge between Europe and Latin America.
description: Adolfo Suárez Madrid–Barajas Airport (LEMD) is Southern Europe's primary international aviation hub. Anchored by the architectural Terminal 4 and T4S satellite complex, Madrid–Barajas provides unmatched long-haul connectivity between Europe and Central/South America.

name: Josep Tarradellas Barcelona–El Prat Airport
shortDescription: Catalonia's major gateway and primary operating hub for Vueling Airlines.
description: Josep Tarradellas Barcelona–El Prat Airport (LEBL) sits directly on the Mediterranean coastline southwest of Barcelona. As a high-density regional and international point-to-point hub, El Prat serves as Vueling's main base alongside growing transatlantic operations.

name: Rome Fiumicino Leonardo da Vinci Airport
shortDescription: Italy's primary international hub airport and main home of ITA Airways.
description: Rome Fiumicino Leonardo da Vinci Airport (LIRF) is Italy's largest airport, located along the Tyrrhenian coast. Serving as the primary hub for ITA Airways, Fiumicino features world-class passenger terminal expansions and connects Italy directly to key global destinations.

name: Munich Airport
shortDescription: Bavaria's primary airport and Lufthansa's secondary premium long-haul hub.
description: Munich Franz Josef Strauss Airport (EDDM) is a high-ranking 5-star European airport. Featuring two parallel 4,000-meter runways and an innovative joint-venture terminal (Terminal 2) operated with Lufthansa, MUC delivers efficient secondary hub operations for Star Alliance.

name: Istanbul Airport
shortDescription: A massive intercontinental mega-hub on the Black Sea coast connecting Europe, Asia, and Africa.
description: Istanbul Airport (LTFM) is an ultra-modern global aviation hub situated on the European side of Istanbul. Featuring the world's largest single-roof terminal building and five active runways, IST serves as the primary home base for Turkish Airlines' extensive global route map.

name: Zurich Airport
shortDescription: Switzerland's largest international gateway and central hub for Swiss International Air Lines.
description: Zurich Airport (Kloten) is Switzerland's principal aviation hub. Known for high operational reliability and premium passenger amenities, ZRH utilizes three intersecting runways to serve as the flagship home base for SWISS and Edelweiss Air.

name: Vienna International Airport
shortDescription: Austria's primary airport and pivotal Central/Eastern European transit hub.
description: Vienna International Airport (Schwechat) is located east of Vienna. Serving as the primary home base for Austrian Airlines, LOWW is a key transit point connecting Western Europe with Central and Eastern Europe as well as the Middle East.

name: Copenhagen Airport, Kastrup
shortDescription: The largest airport in the Nordic countries and primary hub for Scandinavian Airlines.
description: Copenhagen Airport, Kastrup (EKCH) is situated on Amager island just 8 km south of downtown Copenhagen. Operating three runways across a central terminal complex, CPH is the largest international hub in Scandinavia, connecting Northern Europe to global destinations.

name: Dubai International Airport
shortDescription: One of the world's busiest international airports and primary home hub for Emirates.
description: Dubai International Airport (OMDB) is a major global aviation super-hub connecting East and West. Featuring Terminal 3—one of the largest building footprints in the world—DXB serves as the main global mega-hub for Emirates and flydubai.

name: Hamad International Airport
shortDescription: Qatar's flagship 5-star international airport and primary base for Qatar Airways.
description: Hamad International Airport (OTHH) in Doha is renowned for world-class luxury, indoor tropical gardens (The Orchard), and operational efficiency. It features two of the longest commercial runways in Middle Eastern aviation.

name: Zayed International Airport
shortDescription: Abu Dhabi's state-of-the-art international gateway and global home of Etihad Airways.
description: Zayed International Airport (OMAA) features the iconic Terminal A architectural complex. Operating as the official home base for Etihad Airways, the airport connects the UAE capital with key transit nodes across Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

name: King Abdulaziz International Airport
shortDescription: Saudi Arabia's busiest airport and primary gateway for Hajj and Umrah pilgrims to Mecca.
description: King Abdulaziz International Airport (OEJN) in Jeddah plays a critical global role as the primary entry point for millions of pilgrims visiting Mecca. It serves as the principal hub for flag carrier Saudia and low-cost carrier flynas.

name: King Khalid International Airport
shortDescription: The aviation gateway to the capital city of Saudi Arabia.
description: King Khalid International Airport (OERK) serves Riyadh and is expanding rapidly under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 initiatives. Situated north of the capital, RUH features two parallel 4,205-meter runways capable of handling all heavy commercial aircraft.

name: Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport
shortDescription: Australia's primary international gateway and historic home base for Qantas.
description: Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport (YSSY) is Australia's busiest airport, located along Botany Bay. Operating under a strict night curfew, Sydney serves as the core hub for Qantas and connects Oceania with Asia-Pacific, North America, and Europe.

name: Melbourne Airport
shortDescription: Victoria's main international airport, operating 24/7 without night curfew restrictions.
description: Melbourne Airport (Tullamarine) is the primary airport serving the Melbourne metropolitan area. Unlike Sydney, Melbourne operates 24 hours a day with four integrated terminal buildings accommodating domestic, regional, and long-haul international routes.

name: Auckland Airport
shortDescription: New Zealand's largest airport and primary international hub for Air New Zealand.
description: Auckland Airport (NZAA) handles the majority of international traffic entering New Zealand. Located on the Manukau Harbour shoreline, AKL is the flagship hub for Air New Zealand and connects the nation to Australia, the Pacific Islands, Asia, and North America.

name: Tokyo Haneda Airport
shortDescription: Tokyo's primary downtown airport and one of the world's busiest domestic and international hubs.
description: Tokyo Haneda Airport (RJTT) is situated directly along Tokyo Bay, offering quick access to central Tokyo. Serving as the primary hub for both Japan Airlines and ANA, Haneda consistently ranks among the world's most punctual and high-capacity airports.

name: Narita International Airport
shortDescription: Japan's primary long-haul international gateway and major Pacific cargo hub.
description: Narita International Airport (RJAA) located in Chiba Prefecture handles a massive share of Japan's international passenger traffic and air freight. It functions as a key transpacific transfer point connecting North America with East and Southeast Asia.

name: Singapore Changi Airport
shortDescription: World-renowned mega-hub, iconic for luxury amenities and primary home to Singapore Airlines.
description: Singapore Changi Airport (WSSS) is globally celebrated for passenger experience, featuring the iconic Jewel entertainment and retail complex. Acting as the premier gateway between Europe, Asia, and Australasia, it is the primary base for Singapore Airlines.

name: Hong Kong International Airport
shortDescription: Built on Chek Lap Kok island, HKG is a top global cargo airport and home to Cathay Pacific.
description: Hong Kong International Airport (VHHH), often known as Chek Lap Kok Airport, operates a three-runway system. It serves as one of the busiest air cargo airports globally and acts as a central aviation hub for the Pearl River Delta.

name: Incheon International Airport
shortDescription: South Korea's premier international gateway and primary hub for Korean Air.
description: Incheon International Airport (RKSI) located west of Seoul is built on reclaimed land between Yeongjong and Yongyu Islands. It features four operational parallel runways and serves as a crucial transit hub across Northeast Asia.

name: Beijing Capital International Airport
shortDescription: The primary flag carrier hub of Air China serving the capital of the People's Republic of China.
description: Beijing Capital International Airport (ZBAA) is located northeast of Beijing's city center. Featuring the massive Terminal 3 built for the 2008 Olympics, PEK is the primary international base for flag carrier Air China.

name: Shanghai Pudong International Airport
shortDescription: Main long-haul international gateway for Eastern China and primary hub for China Eastern Airlines.
description: Shanghai Pudong International Airport (ZSPD) is situated along the coastline in eastern Pudong. PVG handles the majority of Shanghai's long-haul international flights and ranks among the world's busiest freight airports.

name: Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport
shortDescription: Primary global megahub for China Southern Airlines and major Pearl River Delta hub.
description: Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport (ZGGG) serves Guangdong province as a primary passenger and cargo mega-hub. It is the global operational center for China Southern Airlines, connecting mainland China to Southeast Asia, Oceania, and Africa.

name: Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport
shortDescription: The tech-capital hub serving China's Silicon Valley and primary home base for Shenzhen Airlines.
description: Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport (ZGSZ) features an iconic Terminal 3 designed to resemble a manta ray. Situated on the eastern bank of the Pearl River estuary, SZX is an important logistics and passenger gateway for tech-centric South China.

name: Suvarnabhumi Airport
shortDescription: Thailand's main international hub and home to flag carrier Thai Airways.
description: Suvarnabhumi Airport (VTBS) in Samut Prakan province is the principal aviation hub of Thailand. Featuring one of the world's tallest free-standing control towers, BKK connects Europe, the Middle East, and East Asia to Southeast Asian tourist destinations.

name: Indira Gandhi International Airport
shortDescription: India's busiest airport and primary mega-hub for domestic and long-haul international traffic.
description: Indira Gandhi International Airport (VIDP) serves the National Capital Region of New Delhi. Operating four parallel runways, DEL is the principal hub for both IndiGo and Air India, linking South Asia to global destinations.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport
shortDescription: The primary financial-capital gateway of India featuring iconic Terminal 2 architecture.
description: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (VABB) serves Mumbai, India's financial hub. Renowned for its cross-runway layout and art-filled Terminal 2, BOM handles dense domestic and international traffic within tight urban constraints.

name: Kuala Lumpur International Airport
shortDescription: Malaysia's main airport, split between full-service KLIA1 and low-cost klia2 terminals.
description: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (WMKK) located in Sepang district is Malaysia's largest aviation node. Designed around an 'airport in the forest' theme, KUL is a primary Southeast Asian base for Malaysia Airlines and low-cost mega-carrier AirAsia.

name: São Paulo/Guarulhos–Governor André Franco Montoro International Airport
shortDescription: South America's primary international aviation hub and primary base for LATAM Brasil.
description: São Paulo/Guarulhos International Airport (SBGR) is the busiest airport in South America by passenger volume. Serving Brazil's economic heartland, GRU is a major gateway connecting Latin America with North America, Europe, Africa, and the Middle East.

name: Ministro Pistarini International Airport
shortDescription: Argentina's main long-haul international gateway and primary base for Aerolíneas Argentinas.
description: Ministro Pistarini International Airport (SAEZ), commonly known as Ezeiza Airport, serves the Buenos Aires metropolitan area. Located southwest of the capital, EZE handles the vast majority of Argentina's long-haul international flights.

name: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport
shortDescription: Chile's principal airport and global corporate headquarters for LATAM Airlines Group.
description: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport (SCEL) serves Santiago de Chile. Located in Pudahuel, SCL features two parallel runways and a state-of-the-art international terminal, acting as a crucial South American transit node across the Pacific, North America, and Europe.

name: El Dorado International Airport
shortDescription: The busiest airport in northern South America and primary hub for flag carrier Avianca.
description: El Dorado International Airport (SKBO) serves Bogotá, Colombia. High in the Andes at an elevation of 8,360 feet, BOG handles dense domestic networks and serves as a major cargo hub for South American flower exports.

name: O. R. Tambo International Airport
shortDescription: Southern Africa's primary commercial aviation hub, featuring high-altitude long-distance runways.
description: O. R. Tambo International Airport (FAOR) in Kempton Park serves Johannesburg and Pretoria. Sitting at over 5,500 feet elevation, its 4,418-meter primary runway allows fully laden widebody commercial aircraft to depart safely in hot and high conditions.

name: Cairo International Airport
shortDescription: Egypt's primary international gateway and global home hub for Egyptair.
description: Cairo International Airport (HECA) is located northeast of Cairo near Heliopolis. As one of the busiest airports in Africa, CAI acts as a crucial bridge connecting North Africa, the Middle East, and Europe.

name: Addis Ababa Bole International Airport
shortDescription: The primary East African mega-hub and operational center for Ethiopian Airlines.
description: Addis Ababa Bole International Airport (HAAB) in Ethiopia serves as a central transfer hub for intra-African travel and international connections. Driven by Ethiopian Airlines, ADD links Africa to Asia, Europe, South America, and North America.

name: Cape Town International Airport
shortDescription: South Africa's premier tourist gateway serving the Western Cape region.
description: Cape Town International Airport (FACT) is the second-busiest airport in South Africa. Offering direct long-haul links to Europe, the Middle East, and North America, CPT features a unified terminal complex facilitating smooth transfer between domestic and international flights.

name: Mohammed V International Airport
shortDescription: Morocco's primary international hub and main base for Royal Air Maroc.
description: Mohammed V International Airport (GMMN) is located in Nouaceur Province, south of Casablanca. Serving as the primary hub for flag carrier Royal Air Maroc, CMN connects West Africa with Europe, North America, and the Middle East.

name: London City Airport
shortDescription: Centrally located London airport known for steep landing approaches and business travel.
description: London City Airport (EGLC) is located in the Royal Docks in Newham, close to Canary Wharf and the City of London. Operating under strict noise restrictions and requiring a steep 5.5-degree approach certification, it serves short-haul business and premium regional routes.

name: Cristiano Ronaldo Madeira International Airport
shortDescription: Famous island airport featuring a dramatic runway platform supported by 180 concrete pillars.
description: Cristiano Ronaldo Madeira International Airport (LPMA) serves the Portuguese island of Madeira. Renowned worldwide for its challenging crosswind landings and striking engineering, its extended runway elevated on ocean pillars accommodates European tourist traffic year-round.

name: Innsbruck Airport
shortDescription: Scenic Alpine airport serving Tyrol, famous for demanding mountain valley flight paths.
description: Innsbruck Airport (LOWI), also known as Kranebitten Airport, is the largest airport in Tyrol, Austria. Nestled deep inside the Inn Valley, it requires specialized captain training due to complex mountain terrain and strong Föhn winds, experiencing heavy winter ski traffic.

name: Svalbard Airport, Longyear
shortDescription: The northernmost airport in the world with scheduled commercial public passenger flights.
description: Svalbard Airport, Longyear (ENSB) is situated on the island of Spitsbergen in the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard, Norway. Built on permafrost with specialized insulation layers, LYR serves as the essential lifeling connecting the High Arctic to mainland Scandinavia.

name: Saint Helena Airport
shortDescription: Isolated South Atlantic island airport noted for extreme wind shear challenges on Prosperous Bay Plain.
description: Saint Helena Airport (FHSH) opened in 2016 to replace commercial mail-ship connectivity for the isolated South Atlantic territory. Constructed on a filled-in valley on Prosperous Bay Plain, flight operations require careful planning due to severe wind shear conditions.

name: Seletar Airport
shortDescription: Singapore's historic secondary airport, serving private jets, business aviation, and regional turboprops.
description: Seletar Airport (WSSL) was Singapore's first international civil airport, completed in 1928. Located in the northeast region, XSP today serves as Singapore's dedicated hub for business aviation, flight training, aircraft maintenance, and regional turboprop passenger services.

name: Memphis International Airport
shortDescription: The global superhub for FedEx Express and one of the world's highest-volume cargo airports.
description: Memphis International Airport (KMEM) in Tennessee is world-famous as the global operational center for FedEx Express. Handling millions of metric tons of air freight annually, MEM operates massive nightly sorting operations alongside regional passenger service.

name: Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport
shortDescription: A critical transpacific air cargo refueling node situated equidistant between Asia and North America.
description: Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (PANC) in Alaska occupies a strategic geographic position within 9.5 hours flying time of 90% of the industrialized world. It serves as a major refueling and cargo sorting node for transpacific air freight carriers.
